clue.text: G Boycott breaks 24 — an astronomical event?

indicators.note: these letters break into the other word, splitting it open and sitting inside

parts.note: the answer to 24 down means immense, which is big
to boycott something is to ban it

explanation.surface: Geoffrey Boycott, the Yorkshire batsman, apparently smashes some enormous cosmic happening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'G Boycott' looks like the cricketer Geoffrey Boycott, but it is the letter G and BAN, which 'breaks' into BIG.
explanation.definitionFit: The theorised explosive birth of the universe is the most astronomical event imaginable; the question mark admits it is a theory.

clue.text: Bird smuggled in Australia?

parts.note: Australians call tight men's swimming trunks '... smugglers', so the small parrot is what such trunks are said to smuggle

explanation.surface: A rare parrot is spirited illegally across the Australian border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Budgie smugglers' is Australian slang for skimpy men's swimming briefs; the clue pretends the bird itself is being smuggled.
explanation.definitionFit: A budgerigar is a small Australian parrot, the bird named in the slang phrase for those snug swimming briefs.

clue.text: Spice Girl drops hands with rage, blowing top

indicators.note: the word drops the letters named, leaving them out

parts.note: R and L stand for right and left hands

indicators.note: losing its top, the first letter is lost from the word

parts.note: rage means anger

explanation.surface: A Spice Girl loses her temper and throws up her hands in fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spice Girl' reads as one phrase, but 'Spice' alone is the definition and 'Girl' starts the wordplay; 'blowing top' takes A off ANGER, giving NGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger is a pungent spice from a root, and was also the nickname of one Spice Girl.

clue.text: Head off? New queen rejected church's observances

indicators.note: something off is not right, so these letters are jumbled
rejected means turned back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen
CE is the Church of England, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A beheading followed by a new queen's rejection of the church's rituals: Tudor history in miniature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off?' rearranges HEAD to ADHE; 'rejected' turns N plus ER into REN.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherence to rules is the keeping of them, and observances are likewise acts of following prescribed customs or rites.

clue.text: European character finally needing car service around 2,000

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word that follows
the service's letters go around the Roman numerals

parts.note: the AA, Automobile Association, is a British breakdown service for motorists
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two thousand is MM

explanation.surface: A European finally gets a car serviced, at a price of about two thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: The AA is the British motoring organisation that rescues broken-down cars.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the third letter of the Greek alphabet, and Greek is a European language, so a European character.

clue.text: Perhaps Trump suppresses young woman model

indicators.note: to suppress is to hold down within, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: the US president is commander-in-chief, CIC, Trump being one example
a lass is a young woman

explanation.surface: Donald Trump stifles a young model, a tabloid scandal in seven words.
explanation.walkthrough: CIC is commander-in-chief, a title held by the US president.
explanation.definitionFit: A classic is a model example of its kind, the standard that others are measured against.

clue.text: Maybe Edward, the academic, changes sides in vote?

indicators.note: in a vote, swapping sides turns a pro, for, into a con, against

parts.note: a professor is a senior academic

explanation.surface: A don switches from supporting to opposing in a ballot, perhaps a man called Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: Pros and cons are votes for and against, so PRO at the front of PROFESSOR gives way to CON.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward the Confessor was the pious English king canonised in 1161, an example of the title.

clue.text: Still no place for tart

indicators.note: no here means the named letters are not there

parts.note: still water is calm, placid

explanation.surface: A dessert tart remains homeless, with still no place to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb but is the adjective meaning calm.
explanation.definitionFit: Tart means sharp-tasting, and an acid taste is sour in just that way.

clue.text: Winter dance party is to be thrown!

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a ball held in the snowy season
a packed lump of snow is made to be thrown at someone

explanation.surface: An invitation to a winter ball, exclaimed in excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Split in two the word is a winter ball; whole, it is a missile of packed snow made for throwing.

clue.text: Catholic man's wages for service in county

parts.note: a man is he, so man's gives he's
hire is payment for the use of a service or for work

explanation.surface: A Catholic worker's pay for a church service somewhere in the county.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheshire is a county in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an English shire in the north-west, famous for its cheese and grinning cat, so a county.

clue.text: Biblical character had hassle over vacant inn

indicators.note: over here means placed around the other piece
to hassle is to push around, here turning the word round

parts.note: the word had as written

indicators.note: vacant means emptied, keeping only the outside letters of the word

explanation.surface: A Bible figure has trouble over an empty inn, echoing the nativity's no room at the inn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hassle' looks like the trouble in the story but only turns the word round; 'over' puts it around the emptied inn.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinah was the daughter of Jacob and Leah in the Book of Genesis, a biblical figure.

clue.text: Fabulous creature married fairytale creation

indicators.note: a fairytale is made up, so these letters are invented anew

explanation.surface: A fabled beast weds a creation out of a fairytale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fairytale' rearranges CREATION to ANTICORE.
explanation.definitionFit: The manticore is a mythical beast with a man's head, lion's body and scorpion's tail, so a creature of fable.

clue.text: Wasted one beer and it's spilled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: spilled letters are scattered and land in a new order

explanation.surface: Drunk on one beer, and it ends up spilled everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of "it's" reads as 'is', a link; 'spilled' scrambles BEER AND IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasted is slang for very drunk, the same state as being intoxicated.

clue.text: Portion of fish abruptly returned with expression of disgust

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the letters are read in reverse
a portion is a part, so the letters are taken from inside these words

explanation.surface: A piece of fish is sent back sharply with a cry of disgust, a restaurant complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Portion of' takes HAB from fisH ABruptly; 'returned' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bah is an exclamation of contempt or disgust, like 'humbug' or 'pah'.

clue.text: Primarily, they see close in order to gain a little bit of perspective

definitions.text: Primarily, they see close in order to gain a little bit of perspective

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so the first letter of the word
the jumble gains a letter inside it
put in order, these letters are rearranged
a little bit means just the first letter

explanation.surface: Optical instruments described by what they do: bring the far away close and open up a view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges SEE CLOSE, which 'to gain' a P from 'a little bit of perspective', after T from 'Primarily, they'.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers' instruments make distant objects look near, which is how they let us see close up.

clue.text: Buries Bowman with HAL's core, right between the stars

parts.note: to inter is to bury, so buries gives inters
William Tell, the Swiss folk hero, was a famous archer

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central letter, here of the computer's name in 2001

explanation.surface: In 2001: A Space Odyssey, the computer HAL tries to dispose of astronaut Dave Bowman deep in space.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowman suggests the 2001 astronaut, but it is the archer William Tell.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter- means between and stellar means of stars, so it describes the space lying among them.

clue.text: Since the trouble storing uranium, we get life science

indicators.note: storing means keeping within, so one piece holds the other
troubled letters are stirred up into a new order

parts.note: U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Since the nuclear mishap with uranium, people have taken up biology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges SINCE THE; 'storing' puts U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Euthenics is the study of improving human wellbeing through better living conditions, a science of life.

clue.text: Sobers up, provided inside: lager brewed by daughter

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other
brewed letters are mixed up as in making beer
in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: provided means if, as in 'provided it rains'

explanation.surface: Someone sobers up after a lager made by their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sobers up' looks like recovering from drink; Sobers is the cricketer, and 'up' reverses IF.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Garfield Sobers is the great West Indian cricket all-rounder, so the first name stands for him.

clue.text: Delirious that Conservative's still supporting Europe

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means placed underneath

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative; the 's is 'is', a link
static means still, motionless

explanation.surface: A Tory delighted that the party still backs Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporting' puts the C and STATIC below E in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Delirious can mean wildly excited and happy, the same as being in raptures.

clue.text: Language of Pythagoras?

parts.note: the mathematician of Samos spoke the tongue of classical Greece; the question mark hints at his triangle-theorem jargon

explanation.surface: A question about what the theorem's author spoke, or about mathematical jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: Pythagoras lived in the sixth century BC and spoke the Greek of antiquity, the old classical tongue.

clue.text: In Austria, logician assumes 1 + 1

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so the logician takes the numeral inside

parts.note: John Venn, of Venn diagrams, was an English logician
I is the Roman numeral for one
A also means one, as in 'a day'

explanation.surface: An Austrian logician takes for granted that one plus one makes something.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 1 is the Roman numeral I; the second is the article A, meaning one.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital city of Austria, so a place found in that country.

clue.text: Hurt leg and rear

parts.note: to leg it is to run off, so leg gives off, as in 'be off'
the rear is the end, the back part

explanation.surface: An injury to the leg and backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leg' is slang for going off on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurt someone's feelings is to upset or affront them, the verbal sense of the answer.

clue.text: Highly attractive and flirts regularly

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A good-looking person who flirts as a matter of habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes F, I and T from fLiRtS.
explanation.definitionFit: Fit is British slang for sexually attractive, as in 'he's really fit'.

clue.text: Romantic hero's passion to steal back female

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is', so the definition is the hero

parts.note: heat is passion, as in the heat of the moment

indicators.note: back means the letters run backwards

parts.note: to filch is to steal

explanation.surface: A romantic hero's passion leads him to snatch back a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the synonym for steal; the 's after hero reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathcliff is the brooding hero of Emily Brontë's Wuthering Heights, a Romantic novel.

clue.text: It's mixed into cocktails, at first

definitions.text: It's mixed into cocktails, at first

indicators.note: mixed letters are shaken into a new order
at first means the opening letter of the word

explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges INTO to TONI; 'at first' adds C from cocktails.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is a mixer poured into drinks such as gin and tonic.

clue.text: Immense grip by snake's tail

parts.note: a hug is a tight grip

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter, here the end of the reptile's name

explanation.surface: A boa constrictor's tail gives a crushing grip.
explanation.definitionFit: Immense means extremely large, a straightforward synonym for enormous.

clue.text: Bump into bastard touring Russia, pursuing old girlfriend

clue.text: A vice president makes very little money

definitions.meaning: Mike ... was vice president of the United States under Donald Trump
pennies, the smallest coins of British currency

clue.text: Noble's half-eaten food sent back by Nazi

definitions.note: the 's reads as 'is', so the definition is the noble

clue.text: American sailor tucks into extremely cold or hot sauce
